entries: Plan verification: the PTA confirms the goals and safety limits set by the physical therapist. Execute the prescribed treatment per state licensure and institutional supervision.
Patient observation: the PTA watches for pain, fatigue, and functional changes before and after treatment. Stop the exercise on abnormalities and report to the physical therapist.
Treatment implementation: the PTA assists with exercises, gait, and balance training. Do not diagnose independently or redesign the plan.
Treatment area preparation: the aide cleans surfaces and arranges equipment and supplies. Do not describe logistical support as treatment.
Flow and appointments: the aide assists patient transport, scheduling, and forms per process. Treatment judgments are handed to qualified personnel.
Records and handover: both roles must faithfully record the work they completed. The PTA records patient treatment responses, and the aide hands over the environment and arrangements.
